title: Egg Omelet with Cheese, Meat and Vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: An omelet or scrambled eggs enriched with cheese, meat and vegetables (excluding dark‑green leafy vegetables and tomatoes) is cooked in fat. It is a nutrient‑dense dish providing protein, fats and a range of vitamins and minerals, suitable for breakfast or a light dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are an excellent source of fully digestible protein.
Cheese adds calcium and vitamin D, enhancing flavor richness.
Meat (e.g., ham or chicken) boosts iron and vitamin B12 content.
Vegetables such as bell pepper, onion and mushrooms contribute vitamin C and B‑group vitamins.
The cooking fat improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K).

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Eggs and meat supply all essential amino acids, supporting tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: B2, B6 and B12 support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D from cheese
items.content: Help maintain strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Antioxidants from vegetables
items.content: Vitamin C and other phytochemicals protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Improved nutrient absorption
items.content: Fats used in cooking aid the uptake of fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: Egg or dairy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Excessive use of butter or oil and cheese can raise cholesterol levels if consumed frequently.

items.title: Sodium from meat and cheese
items.content: High salt intake may contribute to elevated blood pressure.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked eggs may contain Salmonella; ensure the mixture is fully set.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Beat eggs with a splash of milk, stir in grated cheese, diced meat and vegetables. Heat a skillet, melt a small amount of butter or oil, pour in the egg mixture and cook over medium heat, gently stirring until the omelet is set but still tender.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed fresh. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat with a little extra fat to retain moisture.
